name: Pinpoint Cafe
notes: Restaurant's own site (pinpoint-cafe.com) has a Wix 'Restaurants' menu widget at /menus that is still unedited template placeholder content ('This Is Your First Item', etc.) and was discarded as not a real menu. The actual first-party ordering platform is Square Online at pinpoint-cafe.square.site, linked from a joe.coffee directory listing for this cafe ('Order on Square'). Square's storefront is a pure client-side SPA with no priced HTML/JSON in a plain curl -- read from the live DOM in the shared browser pane after scrolling to force its virtualized list to render (curl and a first, un-scrolled DOM read both missed the lower half of the menu). Confirmed this beats the DoorDash listing on markup grounds: DoorDash prices for the same items (e.g. Keto Coffee 16oz $7.25, Espresso Over Ice $3.20-$4.20 low end $3.20) match this Square storefront's prices divided by ~1.25 almost exactly (Keto Coffee $5.80 here vs $7.25/1.25=$5.80; several EXTRA-type DD items landed on clean round dollars only after /1.25), so DoorDash was rejected as carrying a 25% delivery markup and this first-party storefront was used instead. joe.coffee's own partial 5-item price sample (Cortado $5.25, Flat White $5.75, Keto Coffee $5.80, etc.) matches this Square storefront exactly and serves as the cross-check. Captured 43 priced items across 7 real categories: Special Drinks, Espresso Drinks, Coffee Drinks, Not Coffee, Frozen Treats, Ice Blended Drinks, Toast. Dropped the 'Shop' section (tote bags, mugs, hoodies -- retail merchandise, not food) and the 'Most Popular' carousel (a duplicate sample of items already in the real sections). Several items are priced by required size (shown as a range on the storefront); the low end of the range is recorded as the price and description says so.

notes: Restaurant's own Squarespace site (kakawacoffeesd.com/menu) publishes full item names, descriptions and sizes but the price field template is broken/unfilled -- every price slot renders as a bare currency sign followed directly by the OZ size label with no digit price (e.g. '$16oz'), confirmed by grepping the whole page for any '$' followed by a real numeric price: zero matches. So the restaurant's own site has no usable prices and was not used as the source. Found a white-label order.online storefront (order.online/en/store/-526755) instead; its RSC flight payload carries 70 MenuPageItem records (10 duplicated in a 'Most Ordered' carousel, 60 unique) and 11 MenuBookCategory entries with per-category item counts. Extracted by collapsing the payload's escaped-JSON-string layer and regexing name/description/displayPrice, then assigning each of the 60 unique items to its section by walking them in payload order against the category item counts (25 Espresso, 5 Tea, 3 Blended, 6 Cold Brew, 1 Smoothie, 3 Kakawa Signature Roast, 1 Coffee Traveler, 7 All Days Eats, 7 Sweet Moments, 2 Gluten Free -- sums to exactly 60, no leftover). Address in the payload (3655 Voltaire St, San Diego, CA 92106) matches the batch. Markup test against 1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25 divisors: no dominant landing (best 11/60 at 1.25, ~18%), so treated as usable at medium confidence per the source ladder for a white-label delivery storefront.

name: Little Chef
notes: Restaurant's own site (littlechefcatering.us) is an unedited template: its only 'order online' links are boilerplate placeholders (an unrelated Ann Arbor 'Chopped NYC' store link, and a generic Chinese-food search results page), and the page has zero real prices. Its Toast directory profile (toasttab.com/local/...) is a business-info listing, not a storefront, and had no ordering link or menu data. Used order.online's white-label storefront for the correct branch instead (URL slug names Ocean Beach, matches batch address of 4910 Newport Ave). RSC flight payload confirmed address (Newport) and gave 121 MenuPageItem records across 13 MenuBookCategory entries; items assigned to sections by walking the flat item list against each category's stated item count. 'Most Ordered' (10) and 'Top 10 Popular' (10) carousels were diffed against the 11 real named sections and every single item in both carousels also appears in a real section, so both were dropped with nothing unique lost. Kept 88 items across 11 real sections: Menu Hacks (Popular Creation), Appetizers, Bbq Pork, Beef, Chicken, House Special, Shrimp, Soup, Vegetable, Bottled Drinks, Extra Sauces On The Side. Markup test against 1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25 divisors found no dominant landing (best 15/88 at 1.1, ~17%). Two prices (Mongolian Beef $16.25, Orange Chicken $14.85) independently match figures quoted in third-party search snippets, supporting these as real menu prices rather than a delivery markup.
